groups.summary: All members reproduced. Element._make_attrs stores the HTML 'class' attribute as 'class_', so get('class') and el['class'] return None. Element.__setattr__ checks key[1:] instead of '_'+key, so `el.tree = x` writes attrs['tree'] and never reaches the @tree.setter. copy, deepcopy and pickle recurse through the deprecated __getattr__ into RecursionError. highlight_overlay's getattr(self, '_is_highlighted', False) goes through the deprecated __getattr__. Only the get('class') member is likely to matter in practice; the others are niche.

member_verdicts.note: Real Chromium, <div class='foo bar'>: get('class') returns None, get('class_') returns 'foo bar', and the attrs keys are ['id','class_']. No test or doc mentions class_. get() was added in 5d15cc7 as the replacement for __getattr__, and get('class') has returned None since then. Nothing shows this is deliberate.
Duplicate of A8.12. Pure Python: get('class') returns None, el['class'] returns None, and repr shows class="btn primary" because __repr__ maps class_ back to class. This is the same root cause.

Pure Python: after el.tree = doc, el.tree returns None, _tree is None, the attrs keys are ['id','class_','tree'], el.parent raises 'element has no tree set', and repr() (which save_to_dom sends to the DOM) contains tree="Node(...)". No caller in zendriver/core assigns .tree, so this hits only users who follow the create() docstring. Realism is low.
Duplicate of A8.14, with the same reproduction. The key[1:] code dates from the initial import 5c1a005.

copy.copy, copy.deepcopy and pickle round-trips of an Element (built with a FakeTab) all raise RecursionError. Refute angle: deepcopy and pickle of an Element bound to a real Tab would fail anyway on the websocket and asyncio objects (assumed, not run), so only copy.copy loses a working result. Realism is low.

With warnings.simplefilter('error', DeprecationWarning), highlight_overlay() raises DeprecationWarning 'Call to deprecated method __getattr__' before sending any command (0 commands sent). With 'always' it records the warning and sends 3 commands. Refinement: with Python's default warning filters in a plain script, nothing is shown, because the warning is attributed to zendriver.core.element and not to __main__. It only appears under pytest's summary, -W or dev mode. The Tab.query_selector(_all) getattr(_node, '__last') path has the same issue but runs only on the 'could not find node' retry path (reasoned only, not run). In normal use this is cosmetic.

groups.summary: Every member reproduced against real Chromium or in pure Python. save_to_dom sends the unescaped __repr__, which corrupts comments and escaped text and fails on quotes. Handles from DOM.resolveNode are never released and keep removed (detached) nodes alive until navigation. Element and Tab are unhashable. Real Chromium. The #cmt outerHTML becomes '

', so the escaped text is now live markup. #q raises ProtocolException InvalidCharacterError, and the element is left with title="say ". A plain element round-trips correctly.

5000 apply() calls produce 5000 distinct object ids, and the first id still resolves afterwards. Refute angle: handles to the same live node cost about 0 B/call of V8 heap (0.52MB to 0.52MB). The real cost is retention of detached nodes. Replacing a 200KB node 400 times with an apply each time grew renderer USS from 43MB to 136MB, against 21MB to 43MB for the control without apply. The first detached handle was still alive (isConnected=False, textContent length 200018). Memory was freed on reload, back to 55MB. This only matters in long-lived single-page apps that replace nodes without navigating. Realism is medium-low.

set(await tab.select_all('a')) raises TypeError unhashable type: 'Element' (real Chromium). __eq__ dates from the initial import 5c1a005 and no __hash__ was ever defined. The failure is loud, not silent. backend_node_id gives a stable key.

hash(browser.main_tab) and set(browser.tabs) raise TypeError unhashable type: 'Tab' (real Chromium). zendriver's own code keeps sets of TargetIDs, not Tabs, so nothing breaks internally. Only user code that hashes tabs is affected, and the failure is loud.

Real Chromium with a local HTTP server, fetch() reported as ResourceType.XHR. Scenario 1 (nested, '*a.json*' outside '*b.json*'): the outer a.request resolves to b.json, the inner b.request also resolves to b.json, a.continue_request continues b's request, and b.continue_request raises 'Invalid state for continueInterceptedRequest'. a.json was never paused, so the inner Fetch.enable replaced the pattern list. Scenario 2 (inner block exits first): fetch is no longer in manually_enabled_domains but 1 handler is still registered. The next send re-enables Fetch with no patterns, so a resolves with the first paused request and b.json stays paused, leaving window.__b None. A navigation inside the outer block stalls: tab.evaluate of the title timed out after 8s. It completes only after the outer block exits. A second RequestPaused event also raised an unretrieved InvalidStateError in _response_handler. The user-installed RequestPaused handler variant was reasoned, not run. The intercept docstring does not say nesting is unsupported. Realism is medium-low.

Real Chromium: evaluate of 1/0, Math.max(), NaN, -0, 2n**64n and 10n all return None, the same as null and undefined (0 correctly returns 0). With return_by_value=False the values come back as the strings 'NaN' and '10', so a workaround exists. c6260fc (#203) fixed only falsy values. Realism is low to medium; empty Math.max/min results are the most plausible trigger.

Real Chromium: after `async with await zd.start(headless=True) as b:`, b.stopped is False and the Chrome pid is still alive. Three loop iterations left three Chrome processes alive inside the event loop. Refute angle: asyncio_atexit's _atexit_cleanup killed all of them when asyncio.run() returned. The two examples that use the pattern (examples/wait_for_page.py and expect_download.py) are single-run scripts and are only lightly affected. The leak is real for loops that open one browser per job. At loop close the cleanup also logged 'Executor shutdown has been called' for each browser (the atexit profile issue owned elsewhere). Additional: __aexit__'s `raise exc_type(exc_val)` replaced a user exception whose constructor takes 2 arguments with a TypeError.

groups.refinements: These are design-level items with mixed severities. The worst runtime effect is A10.2 scenario 2: inside an outer intercept, every request pauses and the page load stalls until the block exits. A8.13 is bounded by navigation or context destruction and costs almost nothing for repeated handles to the same live node; it matters only when apply, click or update run on nodes that are later removed in a long-lived page. B16.10 is bounded by asyncio_atexit at event-loop close, so single-run scripts are unaffected and per-job loops in one event loop pile up Chrome processes. A8.17 and A7.11 fail loudly with TypeError and never silently. A6.9 has a workaround (return_by_value=False). Browser.__aexit__ and Connection.__aexit__ also rebuild exceptions with exc_type(exc_val), which breaks exceptions whose constructor takes several arguments.

Real Chromium with a local HTTP server, fetch() reported as ResourceType.XHR. Scenario 1 (nested, '*a.json*' outside '*b.json*'): the outer a.request resolves to b.json, the inner b.request also resolves to b.json, a.continue_request continues b's request, and b.continue_request raises 'Invalid state for continueInterceptedRequest'. a.json was never paused, so the inner Fetch.enable replaced the pattern list. Scenario 2 (inner block exits first): fetch is no longer in manually_enabled_domains but 1 handler is still registered. The next send re-enables Fetch with no patterns, so a resolves with the first paused request and b.json stays paused, leaving window.__b None. A navigation inside the outer block stalls: tab.evaluate of the title timed out after 8s. It completes only after the outer block exits. A second RequestPaused event also raised an unretrieved InvalidStateError in _response_handler. The user-installed RequestPaused handler variant was reasoned, not run. The intercept docstring does not say nesting is unsupported. Realism is medium-low.

Real Chromium: after `async with await zd.start(headless=True) as b:`, b.stopped is False and the Chrome pid is still alive. Three loop iterations left three Chrome processes alive inside the event loop. Refute angle: asyncio_atexit's _atexit_cleanup killed all of them when asyncio.run() returned. The two examples that use the pattern (examples/wait_for_page.py and expect_download.py) are single-run scripts and are only lightly affected. The leak is real for loops that open one browser per job. At loop close the cleanup also logged 'Executor shutdown has been called' for each browser (the atexit profile issue owned elsewhere). groups.refinements: These are design-level items with mixed severities. The worst runtime effect is A10.2 scenario 2: inside an outer intercept, every request pauses and the page load stalls until the block exits. A8.13 is bounded by navigation or context destruction and costs almost nothing for repeated handles to the same live node; it matters only when apply, click or update run on nodes that are later removed in a long-lived page. B16.10 is bounded by asyncio_atexit at event-loop close, so single-run scripts are unaffected and per-job loops in one event loop pile up Chrome processes. A8.17 and A7.11 fail loudly with TypeError and never silently. A6.9 has a workaround (return_by_value=False). Browser.__aexit__ and Connection.__aexit__ also rebuild exceptions with exc_type(exc_val), which breaks exceptions whose constructor takes several arguments.
